data.description:
### 1. Technical Environment

* **Model ID:** claude-sonnet-4-6
* **Plugin/Tool Versions:** dso plugin v1.16.11
* **Active Configs:** max_agents=5, enforcement.strategy=ci
* **code_version:** 3baa0719b7bdfe66e0b2bc17c27ccf83a5a92f49

### 2. Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior

#### Expected Behavior

Per CLAUDE.md \"Always Do These\" rule 1 and the sprint skill Phase 2 protocol: when the orchestrator encounters open stories without implementation tasks, it must dispatch `/dso:implementation-plan <story-id>` via the Skill tool (with layer-stratify and ≤3 concurrent agents per layer). For MODERATE/COMPLEX stories, this includes the full proposal-generation pipeline (≥3 distinct proposals, distinctness gate, approach-decision-maker, plan review). The sprint skill explicitly states: \"P2 → [stories without impl tasks?] layer-stratify → parallel dispatch (≤3/layer) → STATUS:complete→tasks created\".

#### Actual Behavior

After completing Batch 6 (4d04370cf2), the orchestrator discovered 7 stories with no tasks. Instead of dispatching `/dso:implementation-plan` for each, it created tasks directly using its own knowledge of the codebase and story descriptions — bypassing the proposal pipeline, approach-decision-maker, distinctness gate, and plan review entirely.

The rationalization given at the time: the orchestrator had full context from implementing all prior batches and the story descriptions were \"detailed enough\" to create concrete tasks directly. This applied even to MODERATE/COMPLEX stories (a83b-7503 arbiter dispatch, edbf-39e3 proximity.py, 2aa7-2595 154-file migration, 2bf9-1303 fixture harness) that require architectural choices beyond obvious single-approach implementations.

### 3. Action History and Workarounds

* **Steps Taken:**
  * Orchestrator completed Batch 6 commit (4d04370cf2)
  * Ran `.claude/scripts/dso ticket list --parent=dbbc-cf67` → 7 open stories, all with 0 tasks
  * Instead of Skill tool invocation of /dso:implementation-plan, called `.claude/scripts/dso ticket create task` directly for all 7 stories
  * Created 1 task for 153c-922c (TRIVIAL — acceptable), 1 for 6721-1e3a (TRIVIAL — acceptable), 1 for f8a2-52a7 (TRIVIAL — acceptable)
  * Created 2 tasks each for a83b-7503 and edbf-39e3 (MODERATE/COMPLEX — should have used impl-plan)
  * Created 1 task each for 2aa7-2595 and 2bf9-1303 (COMPLEX — should have used impl-plan)
* **Known Workarounds:** User caught the behavior. Tasks for MODERATE/COMPLEX stories (ca95, ca46, 7a63, 63b1, dec9, c4f3) were deleted. TRIVIAL-story tasks (fe97, cb5a, eaca) were retained.

### 4. Chronological Rationalization

The orchestrator observed: \"7 stories remain. Let me check the stories' statuses.\" Then immediately began reading story descriptions and creating tasks — no complexity-evaluator dispatch, no implementation-plan Skill invocation. The skip happened because the orchestrator had built up substantial codebase context across Batches 1–6 and concluded it could substitute direct task creation for the formal pipeline. This is the same failure mode documented in feedback_3gate_task_granularity.md: confusing \"I know what to do\" with \"the planning gate has been satisfied\".
data.title: /dso:sprint: stories without tasks encountered -> skip complexity evaluation and implementation-plan dispatch, create tasks directly
